page: Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual server instance within the High Performance lineup. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads per core. System resources include 2.0 GB of memory (yielding 1.0 GB per vCPU), an L3 cache allocation of 16 MB, and 60 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate contrasting compute capabilities. In stress-ng single-core evaluation, the processor scored 3206.39, placing in the top tier (top 10%). However, overall multi-core and complex compute results reflect shared virtualization and low core density, registering a multi-core score of 6339.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 5245.37 (bottom 25%). Memory throughput is also constrained, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom 10% (1240.01) and cached read bandwidth reaching 280.84 GB/sec, though uncached large-block transfers maintain moderate throughput around 41.62 GB/sec for reads and 33.03 GB/sec for writes. Compression benchmarks show balanced performance, with single-threaded gzip reaching 29.59 GB/sec.

Given the shared vCPU design and 2.0 GB memory footprint, the instance presents an economical profile for low-concurrency operations rather than intensive production databases or high-traffic web serving. Database benchmark operations and static web serving throughput landed in the lower percentiles. The server is well positioned for basic microservices, staging environments, CI/CD runners, lightweight task orchestration, and edge utility scripts requiring high single-thread execution bursts alongside fast local NVMe storage access.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-amd is a virtual server instance featuring 2 shared vCPUs across 1 physical core on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It comes bundled with 2.0 GB of system memory, 60 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3206.39. However, the shared core topology and constrained 2.0 GB memory envelope lead to lower multi-core output, reflected in modest PassMark memory and database operation scores. Read and write operations to large memory blocks hold steady at 41.62 GB/sec and 33.03 GB/sec respectively. This instance provides cost-effective utility where extreme resource density is not required, making it suitable for development sandboxes, lightweight microservices, basic automation tasks, and modest web utilities.
